correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, k=1..n-2 and ell=2..n, row independence gives P(given directed cycle)=p^ell, P(Z_v=0-indegree)=q^(n-1), and P(Z_v=0-indegree | cycle)=q^(n-1)((n-1)/(n-2))^ell outside the cycle, zero inside it. The (n)_ell/ell sum proves the exact covariance. Elementary f_ell=(n-ell)A^ell is strictly decreasing for ell>=2, with f_2-n=1/(n-2)>0 and f_3-n=-(2n-3)/(n-2)^3<0. The k=n-1 boundary is deterministic. The independent-arc comparison and fixed-k expansions are derived separately. Exact rational exhaustive enumeration covers 10 (n,k) strata and all ell therein, plus all 4096 Bernoulli graphs at n=4; this is not a substitute for proof.

None of the inspected statements establishes the exact joint covariance of directed zero-indegree vertices with every cycle length or the unique positive 2-cycle length. value.rationale: The exact finite sign boundary is a nontrivial structural dependence classification for two intrinsic directed network observables, distinguishable from marginal counts. Only reciprocation has positive cross-covariance with the number of indegree-zero vertices under fixed outgoing degrees, reversing its sign under independently sampled arcs with matching expected outdegree. All longer feedback cycles have negative covariance, with three-cycles unusually O(n^-2) rather than O(n^-1) when k is fixed. The boundary reflects an exact competition between forced incoming edges on a cycle and enhanced avoidance outside it; the statement is a motivated finite structural lemma, not an arbitrary parameter slice or mere Monte Carlo observation.
